objective: Produce one minimal, review-gated, end-to-end experiment that demonstrates the formal chain as far as it is reachable in this environment (compile -> three independent reviews -> decision -> finalization -> authorization -> run -> receipt -> explicit independent F2 attribution), and that pins the F2 node-processing stage as a separately attributable term which is NOT counted as decision computation time.
context: AUDIT work package, not a research contribution. It adds no algorithm, changes no simulator behaviour, and makes no performance claim.

Design: strict 2-cell paired single factor execution.node_process_delay_s = 0.0 (control) vs 0.05 (f2). execution.compute_delay_s = 0.05 is SHARED by both arms and is deliberately NOT a factor: with it non-zero every decision consumes simulated time, so decision_compute_s is non-zero and the separation is discriminating instead of 0 == 0 (this was revision-1 blocking finding B3). Everything else is shared: links.isl_rate_mbps=10.0, routing.policy=hop, demand csv trace CODE/data/traffic/t1_step5_micro_ab.csv, scenario seed 7 / 8 satellites / 1 plane / duration 40, execution.available_capacity_interval_s=0.1. The compiler enforces that the pair shares controlled_signature and trace identity.

MEASURED ON THIS EXACT DESIGN (local non-formal probe, both arms 6/6 DELIVERED, natural_end true, conservation true): control node_process_s 0.0, labelled decision_compute_s 0.899999999999997, unlabelled the same; f2 node_process_s 0.8999999999999979, labelled decision_compute_s 0.8999999999999979, unlabelled 1.7999999999999958. The unlabelled-minus-labelled difference is exactly the node total, so F2 WOULD be published as decision-computation time if the timeline spans were not supplied. The discriminating identity is therefore real and measured, not asserted.

FALSIFIED CLAIM, now excluded: the end-to-end delay increase is NOT equal to the node total on this fixture. MEASURED ON THIS EXACT R02 DESIGN (compute_delay_s = 0.05 shared): total gain 0.849200279 s against a declared 6 x 3 x 0.05 = 0.900 s; packet 99 carries a node occupancy of 0.15 s but its e2e rises only 0.099999964 s while its holding_wait_s falls by 0.050000000 s, and packet 2 diverts 8.000e-04 s into queue_wait. The figure 0.850000245 s quoted in revision 2 is the R01 design's measurement (compute_delay_s = 0); both measure the same absorption but they are NOT the same design and must never be interchanged. One whole node occupancy is absorbed by a pre-existing holding/ISL-queue wait. Additivity holds only on the contention-free unit fixture (test_f2_single_factor_sweep_moves_only_the_node_term). The adversarial reviewer found this by executing both cells; the brief no longer claims otherwise.

DECLARED LIMITATION 1 (remote route): the f2 arm cannot be executed by the canonical remote runner. F2 hard-requires a timeline sink (kernel.py:1145-1152); remote_job.py:304-309 builds the child command from exactly --config --out --authorization --launch-nonce --expect-run-id and never passes one; run-remote.sh:44 rejects '--'. Both the satellite_drl and adversarial reviewers searched for a passthrough and found none. Runs here use the LOCAL CLI with the same formal binding flags: a degraded substitute that exercises verify_authorization_for_leo_sim_v2_config and writes formal_run.json on natural_end, but carries NO VM provenance.

DECLARED LIMITATION 2 (analysis leg): v2_analysis.py:410-415 requires governance_receipt.json, which only remote_job.py writes (:132, :678, :700); v5 receipts force a VM external launch witness (:440-442, :494-497, :922). A locally executed cell therefore CANNOT be verified by v2_analysis. This batch does NOT run it and does NOT claim the chain closes through analysis. This was revision-1 blocking finding B1/B2.

DECLARED LIMITATION 3 (where the F2 separation lives): v2_analysis does not import metrics_independent at all; the only non-test importers in this repository are this work package's own R03/attribute_f2.py (and its frozen revision-2 twin R02/attribute_f2.py), added precisely because the analyzer does not do it, and another work package's step5_recompute.py, which takes no timeline argument. The separation is produced by PROCEDURE section 5b via R03/attribute_f2.py, on purpose and visibly. This was revision-1 blocking finding B4. DISCLOSURE (round 3): on this fixture the labelled decision_compute_s NUMERICALLY EQUALS the f2 node total, both being 18 x 0.05 s, so the separation is demonstrated by the labelled reading being INVARIANT across arms (0.900 s in the control too), NOT by the two totals differing.

DECLARED LIMITATION 4 (acceptance gate): min_delivered_packets / min_multisat_deliveries / require_data_isl / require_control_delivery live only in the remote runner (remote_job.py:111/:118) and are NOT enforced on the local route used here. The observed fate counts are reported instead. The fixture's 6 packets share ONE source and ONE destination pair, so 6/6 multi-satellite delivery is one geometric route property, not six independent trials.

DECLARED LIMITATION 5 (independence semantics): finalize_decision.py:175-183 checks only the two const:true flags and that (reviewer_id, reviewer_session_id) are not reused. 'producer_and_reviewer_are_distinct' therefore means SESSION-ID distinctness and carries no model, family or institutional semantics. The three roles here were executed by three separate cold-start agent sessions; this is NOT human or institutional review and must not be described as such.

REVIEWER PROVENANCE (recorded verbatim, as R06 does): the three review roles for revision 3 are executed by three separate cold-start agent sessions distinct from the producing session. They are not guaranteed to come from different model families, and no receipt field can attest a family. Any claim of independence beyond session-id distinctness is unsupported.

RELATED AUDIT FINDING, recorded because it bounds this batch: no authorization is required to RUN the simulator at all (__main__.py:282-288 returns None when all three formal flags are absent). What authorization gates is the formal witness, the remote serial gate, and analysis. The compiled field name execution_authorized=false describes the DESIGN, not a run permission.

FREEZE-COMPILE-REVIEW ORDERING (mandatory; learned first-hand in revision 2). receipt.code_sha256() hashes CODE/leo_sim/*.py and the compiled manifest binds that value, so ANY edit under CODE/leo_sim/ after compilation invalidates the matrix for authorization (matrix.py:961 'matrix manifest cells do not derive from request'). The only workable order is: freeze CODE/leo_sim -> compile -> review -> authorize -> run. A post-review recompile invalidates all three receipts, so the two orderings are mutually exclusive by construction.

HARD-WON PLATFORM FINDING, first-hand on this work package: the revision-2 block was caused by exactly the code_sha256 drift that ANALYSIS/PLATFORM-AUDIT-REPORT.md records as blocker B2. It is not hypothetical - it stopped this batch. Any change to CODE/leo_sim/*.py voids every compiled matrix and every issued authorization on that checkout, and no pre-merge guard reports the blast radius.
